lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Good morning Jorge! Thanks for picking up.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hey, yeah, I was waiting for your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Great. So today I'd like to hear how the cooking at home went, check how you're feeling, and pick a goal for next week. Anything you want to add?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Actually, I had a question about what to eat at parties.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How are you doing, really?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hanging in there.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Tell me how the cooking at home went this week.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: It went really well, I actually did it 5 times.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You kept going even on a hard week. That says a lot about you.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you mind if I tell you what some people do?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sure.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Cooking a big pot on Sunday can cover two or three dinners.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll set an alarm on my phone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you cook on Sundays?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: So, not yet. I made a big pot of lentils on Sunday.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Once you decide something, you follow through.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I already told my family about my goal.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's completely your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is your daughter able to help?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, I think so. I put a reminder on the fridge.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You already did the hardest part, which is starting.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I put a reminder on the fridge. My doctor said the same thing.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Whatever you pick is fine with me. It's your plan.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What do you think the next step should be?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'm going to do it Monday, Wednesday and Friday. My daughter keeps reminding me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You have to make this a priority.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You have to stop eating out so much.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Well, I'm too tired for this right now.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: On one hand, the cost makes it really hard. On the other hand, you still want to make this work.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay, this week I'll really do it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What did you notice on the days it went well?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Well, my kids is why I'm doing this.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Would it be okay if I shared something that's helped other people?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sure.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Cooking a big pot on Sunday can cover two or three dinners.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay, this week I'll really do it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Part of you is already moving, and you want to keep that going.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I can probably manage three days.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: That's real progress.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: If you don't do this, your health is going to suffer.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, but you don't know my schedule.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You've tried before and it didn't stick.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: After treatment I had no energy at all. Some days are better than others.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What feels doable for next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe cook at home 4 nights?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: If being so tired gets in the way again, what's your backup plan?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll eat a bigger lunch so I'm not starving at night.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Let me make sure I got it. This week you did it 5 out of 5 days, the hard part was the cost, and next week you're going to cook at home 4 nights. Did I miss anything?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, and I'll really try this time.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Same time next Wednesday?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Perfect.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay Jorge, have a good rest of your day.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Thanks, bye bye.

tags.note: Reports 5 days of cooking, strong change talk
Reflects movement and desire to continue
Summarizes plan and checks for missed items

flags.reason: Directive 'You have to make this a priority' without permission; undermines autonomy.
Repeated directive 'You have to stop eating out'; participant responds with sustain talk.
Repeats earlier advice verbatim without new permission or participant interest.
Health-threat warning pushes change and increases resistance; participant pushes back at line 47.
Points out past failure, confrontational and discouraging rather than exploring barriers.
Party-eating question raised at line 4 was never addressed.
Participant reports no energy after treatment; coach did not explore fatigue or wellbeing further.

score.summary: Jorge reported strong cooking progress and Monday/Wednesday/Friday commitments, and the coach set a concrete next-week goal with a barrier plan and summary. However, the coach leaned on directive persuasion (lines 29, 31, 46, 48) and repeated advice (line 40), which drew sustain talk and left his fatigue and party-eating question unexplored.
strengths: Line 10 affirms persistence on a hard week, reinforcing self-efficacy.
Line 33 is a well-crafted complex reflection capturing cost barrier and desire to make it work.
Line 42 reflects movement toward change with added meaning.
Line 52 explores a backup plan for fatigue, a good barrier-planning move.
Line 54 summarizes the plan and invites correction before closing.
coaching_tips: Replace lines 29 and 31 with a reflection or question, e.g., 'What would make eating out less of a stretch for you?' rather than 'You have to...'.
Drop the health warning at line 46; instead ask permission first, e.g., 'Would it be okay to talk about what's at stake for your health?'
Do not repeat advice verbatim (line 40); offer it once and ask what fits his schedule.
Return to the party-eating question from line 4 and the 'really' check-in from line 5 before setting goals.
Explore the post-treatment fatigue in line 49 with an open question about energy and how he's coping.
